courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Business Ethics and Entrepreneurship
courses.description: This course is designed to provide students with an opportunity to study independently start-ups and existing businesses in Hong Kong and the Mainland. Through this course, students learn to (i) integrate and apply their knowledge acquired from different areas and (ii) appreciate how strategies, innovation, corporate social responsibility and business ethics play a role in the development of a business model which adds values to business.
courses.course_syllabus: Student-oriented teaching (STOT) is a small group, less structured teaching which relates to the student’s major field but not necessarily ties to any particular course. This course is designed to provide students with an opportunity to study independently on some selected business and ethical issues in Hong Kong and the PRC. Through this course students learn to integrate and apply their knowledge acquired from different areas.
courses.feedback_evaluation: Students are welcomed to provide comments and feedback to the instructor via email and appointment.

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Accounting Practicum and Fieldwork
courses.description: This course is designed to provide students with professional knowledge and experiences in real-life environment. Practicum and non-local fieldwork/training programs will be arranged to help students link theoretical knowledge to business practices. Students should submit two written reports on the internship experience and the training programme respectively. These reports address topics such as comparative studies of business practices, practical problems encountered in work environment, ethics and corporate social responsibilities. In addition, performance feedback from employer will form part of the assessment.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Not for students who have taken ACCT3001
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of this course, students are expected to be able to:
1. integrate and apply theoretical knowledge and skills acquired to real-world business environment
2. be aware of the importance of business ethics and responsibilities that individuals and companies must assume in business and society
3. understand differences in business practices and culture
4. communicate effectively and efficiently in a professional way
5. explore career options, and gain general work experience
courses.course_syllabus: Practicum and non-local fieldwork/training programs will be arranged to help students link theoretical knowledge to business practices. Students should submit two written reports on the internship experience and the training programme respectively. These reports address topics such as comparative studies of business practices, practical problems encountered in work environment, ethics and corporate social responsibilities.

Tailored questionnaire

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Accounting Field Study and Experiential Learning
courses.description: The course is designed to expose students to a wide spectrum of global accounting related issues in a non-local business environment. Students will take a residential programme in countries or regions outside Hong Kong. Course learning activities may include lectures at universities, case projects, seminars and discussions with local accounting professionals and/or government officials, and site visits to enterprises.
courses.learning_outcomes:
After completion of this course, students are expected to be able to:
CLO1 understand accounting practices and business culture in a global environment
CLO2 understand the operation of one or more functional areas of different enterprises and the roles of accounting
CLO3 communicate effectively and efficiently in a professional way
courses.course_syllabus:
(1) Classroom lectures
Students will take classroom lectures at universities in the visiting countries and regions. The purpose of classroom lectures is to help students understand local and/or global accounting standards, practices and issues.

(2) Group case project
Students will be required to study business models of the enterprises they will visit and present their findings to the class. The purpose of the group case project is to help students better understand the enterprises and relevant industries, and learn more about the roles of accounting in businesses.

(3) Visits to enterprises
Visits to enterprises will be arranged. Through these visits, students have chances to know about the operating process, accounting practices and business cultures of real-world enterprises. They also have chances to talk to the management of those enterprises.
courses.feedback_evaluation: Students are warmly welcomed to provide comments/feedback on the course by sending e-mails to the course instructor and/or making appointments with the course instructor.
courses.required_readings: Reading materials will be provided by the teacher according to the field study.

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Advanced Financial Accounting Studies
courses.description: This course deals with advanced topics of financial accounting. It examines the accounting principles and standards related to group reporting, non-corporate entities as well as other issues. Major topics include business combinations, consolidated financial statements, intragroup transactions, associates, joint ventures and foreign currency translation. This course also contributes to students’ undergraduate capstone experience by helping them (1) integrate business knowledge and generic skills; (2) think from the perspective of a professional and ethical accountant; and (3) transition to the real-world business environment.
courses.course_syllabus:
This course is a continuation of financial reporting and deals with the more advanced aspects of financial accounting. The course assumes knowledge acquired in previous financial reporting courses and thereby focuses on the exploration of the core technical capabilities to prepare and analyse financial reports for combined entities. It takes the subject into greater depth and contextualises the role of accountant as a professional financial adviser by examining the group reporting requirements as well as the rationales behind various accounting principles and standards relating to group reporting.

This course attempts to investigate issues relating to group reporting and therefore includes such topics as business combinations, consolidations of subsidiaries, intragroup transactions and foreign currency translation. Special problems in the consolidation of corporate financial statements will also be covered in the course.
courses.feedback_evaluation: Students are encouraged to provide feedback on the course. Feedback can be sent to the instructor through either email or message system in the eLearning platform at any time or made an appointment with the instructor. Formal teaching evaluation exercise will also be performed at the end of the semester.
courses.required_readings: N/A

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Accounting Information in Capital Market
courses.description: This course establishes a framework for evaluating accounting choices and categorizing the strength of authority for particular accounting treatments. This is accomplished by exposing the students to empirical accounting research and by creating an awareness of the endogenous factors affecting accounting decisions. Major themes are the integration of cash flow and accrual based measures of income from a theoretical perspective and the synthesis of accounting choice questions based on the asset valuation versus income measurement dichotomy. The end result will be a deeper understanding of both the structure and the process of accounting policy-making.
courses.learning_outcomes:
After completing this course, students should be able to:

(1) Identify theories that shape accounting,

(2) Explain predicted accounting behavior based on underlying theories

(3) Critically analyze controversial accounting issues.
courses.course_syllabus:
1. Introduction to Accounting Information in Capital Markets

2. Accounting under Ideal Conditions

3. Decision Usefulness Approach to Financial Reporting

4. Efficient Capital Market

5. The Information Approach to Decision Usefulness

6. The Measurement Approach to Decision Usefulness

7. Measurement Application

8. Economic Consequences and Positive Accounting Theory

9. An Analysis on Conflict of Interest

10. Executive Compensation

11. Earnings Management
courses.feedback_evaluation: Students are welcomed to send their comments/ feedback to the course instructor. The channels include: (1) e-mails to the instructor; (2) appointment with the instructor; and (3) formal CTE exercise.
courses.required_readings: N.A.
courses.recommended_readings: 1. **William R. Scott,** Financial Accounting Theory, Pearson

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: China Business Valuation and Analysis
courses.description: The primary objective of this course is to investigate in depth the current issues in analysing financial statements of Chinese listed firms. It will focus on the analysis of the impact of institutional factors on financial statements, including accounting standard setting, auditing practice, legal and corporate governance, and stock market development. It will examine in depth managerial incentive in accounting choice and estimates. The course will also utilize modern tools and techniques of financial statement analysis through cases assignments and discussions in class.
courses.learning_outcomes: By the end of the course, students should be able to use financial statement data to measure the value of companies in China.
courses.course_syllabus: This course introduces students to issues in business valuation and analysis. It integrates theories and practices of accounting, economics, finance and strategy. A brief discussion of economic determinants and valuation implications of accounting, standard setting, auditing and corporate governance is followed by the examination of economic motivations and valuation implication of corporate decisions including accounting strategy, disclosure strategy, financing strategy, investment strategy and restructuring strategy.

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Applied Financial Statement Analysis
courses.description: This course provides students with the conceptual background and analytical skills that are necessary to identify, assess and apply information for purposes of analysing and valuing business activities and entities. Emphasis is placed on integrating the use of financial statement and non-financial information, and the application of the concepts of valuation, business policy and financial analysis in business valuation and analysis.
courses.learning_outcomes: To provide a framework for using financial statement data to measure the value of companies; to provide students an environment to improve their communication and presentation skills; and to help students learn how to work effectively within a team.
courses.course_syllabus: Financial accounting statements, performance evaluation analysis, statement notes, stock market factor analysis, accounting strategy analysis, disclosure strategy analysis, investment strategy analysis, revenue generation strategy analysis.

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Strategic Management Accounting
courses.description: This is an advanced course in management accounting examining the role of management accounting systems in strategy formation and implementation and as a potential source of sustainable competitive advantage. The course will provide students with practical exposure to the issues involved in the design and implementation of these systems. It will also explore the structures, tools and procedures available to managers to help motivate, evaluate and reward members of the organization.
courses.course_syllabus:
This is an advanced course in management accounting examining the role of management accounting and control systems in ensuring that the organization’s strategies and plans are carried out. Major topics include management control systems, transfer pricing, performance measurement, incentive compensation systems, and corporate governance.

The objectives of this course are to:

1. Provide students with basic concepts of management control systems;

2. Provide students with practical exposure to the design and implementation of various control structures and tools using management accounting.

This course does not deal with technical details of cost accounting as in ACCT2121 and ACCT3121. Instead, it focuses on applying management accounting in organization control. At a practical level, this course should be of interest to students planning a career in accounting, management consulting, or general management.

courses.title: Internal Auditing and Risk Management
courses.description: This course discusses the changing role of internal auditing in the contemporary organisation. It further investigates the inter-locking relationship among corporate governance, risk management and internal control activities; and highlights how internal auditing can bring values to an organisation from a risk governance perspective and assist top management achieve the firm’s strategic goals. Topics on board governance, risk management process and compliance risk management will also be discussed.

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Forensic Accounting and Audit Analytics
courses.description: The advent of technology and data analytics is posing both opportunities and challenges to the accounting professions. On one hand, stakeholders are demanding a more relevant, efficient and meaningful audit of financial statements, driving the accounting profession to conduct the audit engagements using a more in-depth risk-based methodology. On the other hand, with the increasing incidents of fraud including cyberattacks, there has been a significant rise in the adoption of fraud examination and forensic analytics which is considered as a science used to proactively seek opportunities to prevent and detect fraud, waste and abuse by levering information in corporate data assets. This course combines academic and practical discussions of the following three important interlocking areas, namely, how to utilise analytics in an audit of financial statements, how a fraud examination should be carried out and how companies should respond to cyber risks.
courses.course_syllabus:
Topics include:

(1) An introduction of Audit Analytics and Risk-based Methodology in Financial Audits

(2) Use of Computer-assisted Auditing Techniques (CAATs): Checking for Completeness and Integrity, Search for duplicates and gaps and Data Profiling

(3) Fraud Principles, Fraud Schemes and Fraud Risk Assessment

(4) Fraud Prevention, Detection and Response

(5) Transforming Data in Evidence in a Forensic Investigations

(6) Computer Crimes and Cyber Forensics
courses.feedback_evaluation: Students are welcomed to send their comments/ feedback to the course instructor. The channels include: (1) e-mails to the instructor; (2) appointment with the instructor; and (3) formal CTE exercise.
courses.required_readings:

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Data Visualization in Accounting
courses.description: Accounting can be benefited from the use of ‘big data’ to provide better support for judgmental conclusions regarding bad debts, warranties, estimates of useful lives and salvage values, etc. This course will be a hybrid of a survey of the framework of big data and its uses and the actual manipulation of the data using data analysis software such as Tableau. The course does not rely on a knowledge of computer programming nor deep comprehension of advanced statistical techniques. Rather, this course will be largely hands-on in familiarizing participants with the use of data analysis software. Students will select a business question of interest to explore, obtain the appropriate data set(s), and present conclusions derived from the data.
courses.learning_outcomes:
After completing this course, you should be able to:

(1) Explain how “big data” and “data visualization” can be used in business scenarios
(2) Refine a big data business scenarios into an accounting application of the information (tax, estimates of accruals, revenue projections and forecasting, etc.)
(3) Understand the choices available for visualization of data and differentiate amongst alternatives
(4) Form an analysis of the selected big data and present conclusions obtained in an appropriate visualization
courses.course_syllabus:
Topics included:
1. Overview of Big Data and Data Visualization; Numeric versus non-numeric
2. Design Principles for Effective Presentations; Identification of end users and best practices for effective visual presentations of data
3. Introduction to Analytics with Tableau; Dates, Tables, and Mapping; Selections of Charting Tools for Persuasiveness
4. Planning a “Big Data” presentation
5. Identifying Key Metrics and Indicators
6. Telling the data “story” with visuals and dashboards
7. Refining a project proposal to major influence points
8. Importing and Preparing raw data for analysis and presentation in Tableau
9. Exploratory analysis and dashboard submission for storyboards and storytelling
courses.feedback_evaluation: Students are welcomed to send their comments/ feedback to the course instructor. The channels include: (1) e-mails to the instructor; (2) appointment with the instructor; and (3) formal CTE exercise.

Amongst others it will include an examination of the role and functions of the various regulators in the banking, insurance and securities industries; the supervision of and compliance by intermediaries; the protection of investors as well as highlighting of current issues that affect the standing of Hong Kong as an international financial centre.

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Corporate Governance
courses.description: This course introduces and analyses important corporate governance issues and their causes and consequences, with an emphasis of emerging markets and transitional economies. Topics include the effects of institutional factors on corporate governance, corporate ownership structures and managerial incentives, corporate governance issues of different organizational forms, various corporate governance mechanisms adopted for enhancing corporate governance, and the effects of corporate governance in accounting. Students seeking a career in accounting, finance, commercial law and management should find this course interesting and relevant.
courses.learning_outcomes:
By the end of the course, students should be able to
(1) understand the important institutional and human factors in business operations that are often not considered in traditional courses
(2) acquire the concept on the different governance issues and practices in these markets.
courses.course_syllabus: The course covers important corporate governance issues and their resolutions through lectures, case studies, and discussion of contemporary research and public opinions. Topics covered in this course include the importance of institutional factors (such as public governance and legal protection) in corporate governance, corporate ownership structures and managerial incentives, corporate governance issues of family firms and state owned enterprises, corporate governance mechanisms (boards of directors and executivee compensation), corporate transparency and corporate accounting reporting.
courses.feedback_evaluation: Students are welcomed to provide comments and feedback to the instructor via email, appointment and the CTE exercise.
courses.required_readings: Kenneth Kim and John Nofsinger, 2004, Corporate Governance, (Prentice Hall), KN here after.
courses.recommended_readings: It is expected that you will be an aggressive reader of business publications (Chinee or English), including Xin Pao, The New Fortune, Cai Jin, The 21st Century Economic Report, The Asian Wall Street Journal, The South China Morning Post, The Economists, Business Week, and so forth. Please look for opportunities to apply class materials to your reading of the business press and volunteer your observations in class.

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: ESG and Sustainability Accounting
courses.description: This course helps students obtain a broad and critical understanding of how accountants can contribute to an organisation’s value creation through ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) initiatives. The course introduces different theories and perspectives that explain the growing importance of ESG and focusses on how such ESG issues are measured, reported and valued by capital market participants. The course compares major ESG reporting frameworks and their applications in the real world. The course also explores how ESG issues can be integrated into traditional accounting disciplines such as management and cost accounting, internal controls, performance measurement and assurance.
courses.course_syllabus:
1. **An introduction of ESG**
2. **Management accounting and control (MAC) for sustainability**
3. **Measuring and rating CSR/ESG**
4. **Reporting standards of ESG practices and sustainability issues**
5. **Special accounting topics on ESG**

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Business Law
courses.description: This course is designed to develop knowledge and skills in the understanding of the general legal framework and legal issues that arise from day-to-day business activities. Through the study of cases and legislation, it aims to cultivate the analytical skills of students within a legal context. Topics to be covered may include the Hong Kong legal system, contract law, the law of torts, employment law, the formation and constitution of business organizations, capital and the financing of companies, management, administration and the regulation of companies, the winding up of companies, governance and ethical issues relating to business.
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of the course, students are able to:
a) Understand the legal principles, general legal framework and legal issues for business
b) Understand the process of merger and acquisition, rights of minority’s shareholders, and the new competition law
c) Develop analytical skills for business decision within a legal context

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Company Law and Security Law of China
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to the legal system of China’s capital market. Topics covered include: the corporate governance of companies, the process of companies going public, the information disclosure requirement of listed companies, and security trading regulations in China.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MBA in Finance (40087); or MBA in Finance (40324)
courses.learning_outcomes:
Students will:
- be familiar with existing Chinese rules and practices
- be able to identify and compare different conceptions of and approaches to law to bring home systemic problems China has encountered in its modernization efforts
- be familiar with the economic, political and historical backgrounds of company law as well as main provisions of PRC company legislation
- be able to analyse cases concerning various company law issues that have been litigated
- have thorough understanding of problems of securities markets and investor protection as well as theories dealing with those problems
- be familiar with legal issues related to the issuance and transactions of securities as well as liabilities of different actors

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Field Study for Accounting Managers
courses.description: The course is designed to expose students to a wide spectrum of global accounting related issues in a non-local business environment. Students will take at least a week-long residential programme in various countries or regions. Course learning activities include lectures and/or seminars at universities, discussions with local accounting professionals and/or government officials, and site visits to enterprises.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Executive Master of Professional Accountancy
courses.learning_outcomes:
After completion of this course, students are expected to be able to:
(1) understand accounting practice in different countries and regions
(2) understand business models of different enterprises and the supporting role of accounting
(3) communicate effectively in a professional way
courses.course_syllabus:
- Professional seminars in accounting and finance
- Site visits to enterprises
courses.feedback_evaluation:
Students will be asked to complete an evaluation form on the study trip for improvement.
Mandatory Course and Teaching Evaluation (CTE) is conducted at the end of the course.
courses.required_readings: No required readings

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Financial Accounting Theory
courses.description: This course establishes a framework for evaluating accounting choices and categorizing the strength of authority for particular accounting treatments. This is accomplished by exposing the students to empirical accounting research and by creating an awareness of the endogenous factors affecting accounting decisions. Major themes are the integration of cash flow and accrual based measures of income from a theoretical perspective and the synthesis of accounting choice questions based on the asset valuation versus income measurement dichotomy. The end result will be a deeper understanding of both the structure and the process of accounting policy-making.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Accountancy
courses.course_syllabus:
• Introduction, Accounting and the Capital Market
• Accounting Theoretical Framework
• Decision Usefulness
• Efficient Capital Market & Information Perspective
• Measurement Approach
• Measurement Approach: Fair Value Accounting
• Other Applications of the Measurement Approach and Economic Consequences
• Positive Accounting Theory and Earnings Management
• Game Theory
• Accounting and Compensation
• Standard Setting, Nonfinancial Disclosure and Review, International convergence

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Management Control Systems
courses.description: Designed properly, management control systems serve to influence and structure employee behavior in ways that increase the likelihood that organizational objectives are achieved or exceeded. This course provides an advanced-level examination of the alternative control mechanisms available to organizations, theories underlying their use, and their intended and often unintended effects on behavior. Particular attention is directed to the critical decisions underlying the design of effective accounting based control systems including choice of responsibility structure, performance measures, performance standards, and incentive systems, and to emerging issues in corporate governance.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Accountancy; or Executive Master of Professional Accountancy
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of the course, students will be able to:
a) Be equipped with basic concepts of management control systems
b) Understand the design and implementation of various control structures and tools using management accounting
courses.course_syllabus:
• The Basics of Management Control
• Management Control Types, Tightness, Costs, and Design
• Financial Responsibility Centers and Transfer Pricing
• Planning and Budgeting
• Incentive Compensation Systems
• Financial Performance Measures
• Combination of Measures and Myopia Problem
• Financial Results Control and Uncontrollable Factors
• Controllers and Auditors
• Strategy and Adaptation Costs
• Ethical Issues in Management Control Systems
• Control in Nonprofits
courses.feedback_evaluation: Mandatory Course and Teaching Evaluation (CTE) is conducted at the end of the course.
courses.required_readings: Management Control Systems, 4th/3rd Edition. Merchant and Van der Stede, Prentice Hall.
courses.recommended_readings:

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Advances in Strategic Management Accounting
courses.description: This is an advanced course in management accounting examining the role of management accounting systems in strategy formation and implementation and as a potential source of sustainable competitive advantage. The course blends current research with practical exposure to the issues involved in the design and implementation of these systems. Topics include cost of capacity, activity-based management systems for operational and strategic control and contemporary approaches to performance coordination and evaluation in a decentralized environment.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Accountancy; or Executive Master of Professional Accountancy
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of the course, students will be able to:
a) Understand how organizations implement business strategies successfully with effective management control systems
b) Understand how organizations employ strategic cost management tools to develop sustainable competitive advantages

COST ANALYSIS AND STRATEGY
Session 1: Overview of cost systems
Session 2: Cost behavior and theory of constraint
Session 3: Product costing and strategic positioning
Session 4: Activity-based costing and corporate strategy
Session 5: Cost of capacity
Session 6: A taste of academic research

COST ANALYSIS AND NEW PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT
Session 7: ABC and new product development
Session 8: Target costing and new product development

COST ANALYSIS AND MARKETING MANAGEMENT
Session 9: Costing Customers: The banking industry
Session 10: Costing Customers: The healthcare industry
Session 11: Value chain analysis

COST ANALYSIS AND QUALITY/OPERATION MANAGEMENT
Session 12: Half-life system
Session 13: Pseudo-profit center

COST MANAGEMENT AND CORPORATE RESTRUCTURING

Session 15: Managing cost through downsizing
Session 16: Managing cost through buyout

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Assurance Services and Information Technology
courses.description: This course examines Hong Kong legal environment and discusses how it will affect audit risk, audit planning, internal controls, analytical procedures, and substantive tests. Building on this foundation, this course then focuses on information technology and examines its impacts on financial reporting systems. Specifically, we emphasize on how auditors can leverage information technology and use Computer-Assisted Audit Tools and Techniques (CAAT) to attest clients’ financial statements.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For student in Master of Accountancy;Prerequisite: ACCT5130
courses.learning_outcomes:
After taking this course, students are expected to:
1. Understand Hong Kong legal environment and how it affects auditing and assurance services
2. Be familiar with internal control framework, audit risk model, and auditing planning
3. Understand how audit judgments affect evidence accumulation
4. Be familiar with statistical sampling and non-statistical sampling approaches in auditing
5. Understand how to document clients’ business processes
6. Comprehend how to evaluate clients’ internal controls over financial reporting
7. Realize the information security issues related to clients’ accounting systems
8. Be familiar with Computer-Assisted Audit Tools and Techniques (CAAT) and Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP)
9. Understand the relationship between application controls and substantive tests
10. Realize auditors’ responsibilities over client’s fraudulent activities
courses.course_syllabus:
• Hong Kong legal environment and its effects on auditing and professional services
• COSO internal controls framework, audit risk, and auditing planning
• Audit judgment and audit evidence accumulation
• Statistical sampling and non-statistical sampling approaches in auditing
• Business processes and financial reporting systems
• Accounting information systems
• Information security
• CAAT and ERP
• Application controls and substantive testing
• Auditors’ responsibilities over client’s fraudulent activities

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Applied Corporate Governance for Capital Markets
courses.description:
This course equips the students with a deeper understanding of the current state of play as regards corporate governance principles and rules, and the institutions through which corporate governance rules are applied to capital market participants, with a special focus on the Hong Kong and mainland China capital markets, but also addresses the challenges and trends in the real-life market place and how the linkages between effective enterprise governance, risk management and compliance can contribute to superior business performance and thereby to enhanced investor confidence in the capital markets.

Many diverse topics which impact how corporate governance is applied in practice in the capital markets, such as increasing regulatory supervision, GRC, key capital market participants, changes in the structure of the auditing profession, hot business transformation trends, a new enterprise business model, etc, are brought to life in an interlinking way using case studies and visiting business leaders to brief students and answer their questions.

Students are encouraged throughout the course to think about practical solutions to enhance corporate governance practices in Hong Kong and mainland China’s capital markets.
courses.learning_outcomes:
On completion of this course, students are expected to be able to:
1. Demonstrate a deep understanding of the major corporate governance issues around the world;
2. Apply basic economic theories and logic to critically analyze corporate governance issues; and
3. Communicate their analysis and findings in an effective way.
courses.course_syllabus:
• Introduction of corporate governance
• International corporate governance
• Ownership structure and corporate governance in China
• Corporate governance mechanisms (1) - board of director
• Corporate governance mechanisms (2) - executive compensation and incentives
• Corporate governance mechanisms (3) - financial reporting and disclosures, auditing
• Corporate governance mechanisms (4) - the market for corporate control; institutional and activist investors
• Corporate governance mechanisms (5) - financial analysts, media, and regulators
• Corporate social responsibilities and socially responsible investment

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Corporate Governance: An East Asia Perspective
courses.description:
This course identifies the corporate governance challenges for companies in China and East Asia, and explores various mechanisms for strengthening their governance systems. We pay particular attention to the corporate governance issues of state-owned firms and entrepreneurial / family-controlled firms, which are prevalent in China and East Asia.

The course adopts a multi-disciplinary approach, using theories from economics, law, political science and sociology, to provide a theoretical framework for understanding the different ownership structures and corporate governance systems around the world. Combining theories with practical knowledge of corporate governance practice, we tackle issues such as government intervention on state and non-state firms, accounting opacity and fraud, ineffective board monitoring, expropriation of controlling owners against minority shareholders, and succession in family firms.
courses.learning_outcomes:
By completion of the course, students would be able to:
1) understand how various country institutions such as the political economy, legal systems and social norms shape the corporate governance and accounting systems across countries
2) analyze how firms’ corporate governance and accounting systems, which are shaped by their own country institutions, operate across countries
3) identify the challenges and analyze the effectiveness of corporate governance and accounting systems of listed firms across countries, with a focus in Asia and China
courses.course_syllabus: The course will start with a discussion on the recent corporate governance issues in the U.S. and the general theories from economics, finance and law underpinning the study of corporate governance. This is followed by a discussion of how country institutions such as political economy, legal system, and culture and social norms shape firms’ corporate governance around the world. We then focus on East Asia and China, exploring the unique institutional factors that shape their governance systems. We will identify the governance systems’ key advantages and challenges, understand the theoretical reasoning behind the systems and discuss solutions to these governance challenges.
courses.feedback_evaluation: Mandatory Course and Teaching Evaluation (CTE) is conducted at the end of the course.
courses.required_readings: Detailed class notes, and four to five cases, all developed by the instructor.
courses.recommended_readings: The instructor will occasionally recommend articles from business publications including Xin Pao, The New Fortune, Cai Jin, Cai Xin, The 21st Century Economic Report, The Asian Wall Street Journal, The South China Morning Post, The Economist, Business Week, and so forth.

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Accounting and Management Planning for Enterprises
courses.description:
“What distinguishes the successful entrepreneur and promoter from other people is precisely the fact that he does not let himself be guided by what was and is, but arranges his affairs on the ground of his opinion about the future. He sees the past and present as other people do; but he judges the future in a different way." (Human Action, Ludwig von Mises, 1966)

Entrepreneurial activities have become a potent source of economic power that generates enormous job opportunities and business innovation globally. This is particularly spectacular in the context of China where there are numerous cases of successful and failure cases of privately owned enterprises and collectively owned township and village enterprises growing from an embryonic stage into a larger firm. The course adopts a “life-cycle” approach and develops a set of accounting and managerial skills to analyze companies from the start-up stage to eventually cashing out.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master in Accountancy
courses.learning_outcomes:
After taking this course, students are expected to:
1. Understand how to get started with their new venture including:
• Generating business idea to formulating a business plan
• Organizing and financing a new venture
2. Be familiar with the accounting cycle of strategic and business planning
3. Understand more the importance of cost management and budgeting from the perspective of private equity funds
4. Be familiar with the fundamental equation of business including the introduction of an entrepreneurial capital budgeting model and important consideration like capital structure and leverage
5. Consider exit mechanism and strategies for the new venture

Getting started

• Organizing and financing a new venture
• An overview of new venture financing
Financial aspects of strategic and business planning
• The business plan
• New venture strategy
• Cash flow analysis
• Managing profit and financial statements
Financial aspects of strategic and business planning
• Doing due diligence
• Valuations
Organizational design and financial contracting
• Financial contracting
• Information and incentive problems
Financial choices
• Venture capital financing
• Choice of financing
Growing a firm – internally
• A review of fundamentals
• An entrepreneurial capital budgeting model
• Capital structure and leverage
Financing tools
• Raising funds externally: An overview of investment banking
• Long-term financing
• Intermediate-term financing
• Short-term and working capital financing
External expansion – M&A
• Searching for an acquisition
• Technical aspects of acquiring a firm
• Financing and strategic decisions of Chinese companies expanding overseas
Exit mechanism and strategies
• IPO

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Independent Study in Accounting
courses.description: Independent study gives students added flexibility to design study programmes suited to a particular area of interest or to delve more deeply into a specific topic. Students need to find a faculty member willing to serve as the supervisor, and together, devise a format. There are a wide range of possibilities under independent study. The more common alternatives are: (a) Selection of a topic not normally covered in our curriculum in which the student has an interest. Normally the student would prepare a literature review on the selected topic. It would then be common for the student to perform some application or extension of this body of knowledge by extending or substantiating that knowledge by some data collection. (b) Preparation of a case and accompanying teacher’s note. The case must be based on real organizations and substantial data collection would be expected. The student would be expected to demonstrate application of theory in preparation of the teacher’s note.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Accountancy
courses.learning_outcomes: Independent study gives students added flexibility to delve deeply into a selected topic as agreed by a professor. After completing this course, students will be able to: (1) Have an enhanced understanding of a topic not normally covered in our curriculum in which the student has an interest; (2) Have a better understanding of how to carry out an academic research, i.e., preparing literature review; forming hypotheses; extending knowledge via data collection; and, analyzing and interpreting the results; (3) Write a proper research or case report; and (4) Demonstrate a proper application of theory to examine hypothesis.

courses.subject: ACCT
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: The purpose of this course is to expose graduate students to special topics not otherwise covered. Prior to taking this course, students should submit a proposal to and get approval from the instructor-in-charge stating the purposes and major objectives of their study. Details regarding how the study will be conducted are decided through consultation with their instructor-in-charge. The instructor may also ask the students to write reports throughout the semester, for example, a mid-course progress report and an end-of-course final report. This course requires research which is not a significant duplication of the thesis.
courses.learning_outcomes:
By completion of the course, students will be able to:
L1: Master basic theoretical concepts in accounting research
L2: Develop a good understanding of the evolution of accounting research
L3: Assess the validity of research work
L4: Critique accounting research by applying basic accounting theories
L5: Develop a basic work framework for generating new research ideas in a special accounting topic
